page: UpCloud GPU-8xCPU-64GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 8 vCPUs, consisting of 8 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, under a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, featuring 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. This server configuration does not include local storage.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 4092.76 and single-threaded gzip compression at 43.94 GB/sec both rank in the top tier (top 10%). Similarly, single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 19.5 GB/sec, also placing in the top tier. Multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance (32452.12) and PassMark CPU score (27004.32) falling into the average category (middle 50%). Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only large block speeds at 123.85 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 66.29 GB/sec. For AI workloads, LLM inference text generation using a small 135M model achieves a top-tier speed of 402.56 tokens/sec, while prompt processing for the same model operates at an average speed of 1942.23 tokens/sec.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a qualitative balance of GPU acceleration and memory capacity. However, the shared CPU allocation model may introduce performance variability under sustained multi-core loads, and the complete absence of local storage requires external storage attachments. Given the hardware profile and benchmark results, this instance is suited for workloads such as lightweight LLM inference, machine learning model evaluation, single-threaded data compression tasks, and GPU-accelerated graphics or compute workloads that do not demand dedicated CPU cores or local disk space.
